Subject: Route-level cost & SLA exception breakdown (urgent)

Hi Vanessa / Tessa,

We're seeing a recurring invoice variance tied to what our billing team calls “route skews” — specific API routes that spike token counts unpredictably and trigger SLA exception credits. Can Redwood produce: a per-route daily cost breakout (last 90 days), a small dashboard widget we can embed in our internal ops, and a playbook for handling SLA exception investigations (who to notify, what telemetry to collect)?

Our procurement folks would like a short deliverable by next week (by 6/14) so they can reconcile the Q2 forecast. I’ve attached an exported sample of our tenant billing for May to show the pattern.

Key asks:
- Per-route cost and 95th/99th latency percentiles by day
- Flagging rules for routes that would auto-open an SLA exception
- Suggested lightweight dashboard snapshot we can embed in Data Studio (or a CSV template we can import)

Appreciate a quick confirmation of next steps.

Thanks,
Erin
Erin Smith

Vanessa — quick feasibility notes after skimming the sample CSV and infra:  

- Export: we can produce per-route daily aggregates (tokens, cost_usd) and VMs' p95/p99 latency percentiles from current telemetry. The sample maps cleanly to our ingestion, but there are a couple of quirks: some BrightLedger routes are using long prompt templates that cause token bursts and our prefix-caching masks that in aggregated views. I recommend we export both raw per-request token counts (sampled at 10%) and daily aggregates so they can choose.

- Exception flags: we should define two thresholds — a relative anomaly (>=3x baseline for a route week-over-week) and an absolute token threshold per-call (example: >50k tokens) — either can open an SLA exception. Creating both allows the billing team to tune sensitivity.

Action items for me:
- INF-4821: Add telemetry export job and attach CSV schema (target 6/12)
- Share an example raw-sample (10k rows) to Erin by EOD 6/11

Sooj

Thanks — adding a few product constraints and a UX suggestion:  

- UI scope: Instead of a full-blown per-route product page, deliver a "slice-led card" that can be parameterized by route regex and timeframe. The card should show: 7-day sparkline of cost, daily p95/p99 table toggle, and a red/yellow flag column for anomaly state. This keeps dev scope small and reusable.

- Rollouts: we can ship card as an opt-in Console beta feature tied to a flag (console.slice_cards). If BrightLedger needs embedding, we can provide an export URL + CSV consumer endpoint (read-only token).

- SLA automation: Ops can auto-open an exception ticket in our internal Jira (INF-EX-<number>) when the anomaly rule fires; product needs to expose a mapping from rule -> Jira project/assignee. I can scope the UI changes and PR with mockups by 6/12.

Marissa
